- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# dog

**dog** is a command-line DNS client, like `dig`.

It has colourful output, understands normal command-line argument syntax, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.

![A screenshot of dog making a DNS request](dog-screenshot.png)

## Examples

    dog example.net                          Query a domain using default settings
    dog example.net MX                       ...looking up MX records instead
    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1              ...using a specific nameserver instead
    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T           ...using TCP rather than UDP
    dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T   As above, but using explicit arguments

## Command-line options

### Query options

    <arguments>              Human-readable host names, nameservers, types, or classes
    -q, --query=HOST         Host name or domain name to query
    -t, --type=TYPE          Type of the DNS record being queried (A, MX, NS...)
    -n, --nameserver=ADDR    Address of the nameserver to send packets to
    --class=CLASS            Network class of the DNS record being queried (IN, CH, HS)

### Sending options

    --edns=SETTING           Whether to OPT in to EDNS (disable, hide, show)
    --txid=NUMBER            Set the transaction ID to a specific value
    -Z=TWEAKS                Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks

### Protocol options

    -U, --udp                Use the DNS protocol over UDP
    -T, --tcp                Use the DNS protocol over TCP
    -S, --tls                Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol
    -H, --https              Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol

### Output options

    -1, --short              Short mode: display nothing but the first result
    -J, --json               Display the output as JSON
    --color, --colour=WHEN   When to colourise the output (always, automatic, never)
    --seconds                Do not format durations, display them as seconds
    --time                   Print how long the response took to arrive

## Installation

Binary downloads of dog are available from the releases section on GitHub for 64-bit Windows, macOS, and Linux targets. They contain the compiled executable, the manual page, and shell completions.

Package manager installations may also be available:
- For Arch Linux: `dog` package
- For Homebrew on macOS: `dog` formula  
- For NixOS: `dogdns` package

## Documentation

For detailed documentation on how to use dog, see the manual page or visit: <https://dns.lookup.dog/>

# Note: This works for both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and also PowerShell 7 (Core).
# But beware that in Windows PowerShell 5.1, it has issues with completing args if they start with '-'.
# For more information about the bug, see: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/2912
# In PowerShell 7+, it should work correctly.
Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'dog' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    [string]$argsString = $commandAst.ToString()

    # skip the "dog", split the args afterwards as array
    [string[]]$argsArray = $argsString.Split([char[]]@(' ', '=')) | Select-Object -Skip 1
    if ($argsArray -eq $null) { $argsArray = @() }

    # detect if starting a new arg (aka ending with space and asking for a completion)
    [bool]$isNewArg = $cursorPosition -gt $argsString.Length
    if ($isNewArg) {
        # if writing a new arg, add empty arg so that current and previous would be shifted
        $argsArray += ''
    }

    # get current arg (empty if starting new)
    [string]$currentArg = $argsArray[-1]
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($currentArg)) {
        $currentArg = ''
    }

    # get previous arg
    [string]$previousArg = $argsArray[-2]
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($previousArg)) {
        $previousArg = ''
    }

    [string[]]$dnsTypeValues = @('A', 'AAAA', 'CAA', 'CNAME', 'HINFO', 'MX', 'NS', 'PTR', 'SOA', 'SRV', 'TXT')

    [string[]]$completions = @()
    [bool]$isOptionValue = $argsString.EndsWith('=')

    # complete option value
    switch -Regex ($previousArg) {
        '^(-q|--query)'       { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(-t|--type)'        { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += $dnsTypeValues }
        '^(-n|--nameserver)'  { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(--class)'          { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('IN', 'CH', 'HS') }
        '^(--edns)'           { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('disable', 'hide', 'show') }
        '^(--txid)'           { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(-Z)'               { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('aa', 'ad', 'bufsize=', 'cd') }
        '^(--color|--colour)' { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('always', 'automatic', 'never') }
    }

    # detect whether to complete option value
    if ($isOptionValue) {
        if (!$isNewArg) {
            # if using =, complete including the option name and =
            $completions = $completions | ForEach-Object { "$previousArg=$_" }
        }
    } 
    else {
        # if not completing option value, offer DNS type values first
        $completions += $dnsTypeValues

        # complete option name
        [string[]]$allOptions = @(
            '-q', '--query',
            '-t', '--type',
            '-n', '--nameserver',
            '--class',
            '--edns',
            '--txid',
            '-Z',
            '-U', '--udp',
            '-T', '--tcp',
            '-S', '--tls',
            '-H', '--https',
            '-1', '--short',
            '-J', '--json',
            '--color', '--colour',
            '--seconds',
            '--time',
            '-?', '--help',
            '-v', '--version'
        ) | Sort-Object

        $completions += $allOptions
    }

    if ($completions.Count -gt 0) {
        # narrow down completions by like* matching
        return $completions -like "$currentArg*"
    }
}

dog.1.md
% dog(1) v0.1.0

<!-- This is the dog(1) man page, written in Markdown. -->
<!-- To generate the roff version, run `just man`, -->
<!-- and the man page will appear in the ‘target’ directory. -->


NAME
====

dog — a command-line DNS client


SYNOPSIS
========

`dog [options] [domains...]`

**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.


EXAMPLES
========

`dog example.net`
: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings

`dog example.net MX`
: ...looking up `MX` records instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
: ...using a specific nameserver instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
: ...using TCP rather than UDP

`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
: As above, but using explicit arguments


QUERY OPTIONS
=============

`-q`, `--query=HOST`
: Host name or domain name to query.

`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)

`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`
: Address of the nameserver to send packets to.

`--class=CLASS`
: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)

By default, dog will request A records using the system default resolver. At least one domain name must be passed — dog will not automatically query the root nameservers.

Query options passed in using a command-line option, such as ‘`--query lookup.dog`’ or ‘`--type MX`’, or as plain arguments, such as ‘`lookup.dog`’ or ‘`MX`’. dog will make an intelligent guess as to what plain arguments mean (`MX` is quite clearly a type), which makes it easier to compose ad-hoc queries quickly. If precision is desired, use the long-form options.

If more than one domain, type, nameserver, or class is specified, dog will perform one query for each combination, and display the combined results in a table. For example, passing three type arguments and two domain name arguments will send six requests.

DNS traditionally uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP. To use a resolver with a different port, include the port number after a colon (`:`) in the nameserver address.


SENDING OPTIONS
===============

`--edns=SETTING`
: Whether to opt in to DNS. This can be ‘`disable`’, ‘`hide`’, or ‘`show`’.

`--txid=NUMBER`
: Set the transaction ID to a specific value.

`-Z=TWEAKS`
: Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks.


TRANSPORT OPTIONS
=================

`-U`, `--udp`
: Use the DNS protocol over UDP.

`-T`, `--tcp`
: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.

`-S`, `--tls`
: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.

`-H`, `--https`
: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.

By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.

The DNS-over-TLS (DoT) and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) protocols are available with the `--tls` and `--https` options. Bear in mind that the system default resolver is unlikely to respond to requests using these protocols.

Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.

Unlike the others, the HTTPS transport type requires an entire URL, complete with protocol, domain name, and path.


OUTPUT OPTIONS
==============

`-1`, `--short`
: Short mode: display nothing but the first result.

`-J`, `--json`
: Display the output as JSON.

`--color`, `--colour=WHEN`
: When to colourise the output. This can be ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’, or ‘`never`’.

`--seconds`
: Do not format durations as hours and minutes; instead, display them as seconds.

`--time`
: Print how long the response took to arrive.


META OPTIONS
============

`--help`
: Displays an overview of the command-line options.

`--version`
: Displays the version of dog being invoked.


ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
=====================

dog responds to the following environment variables:

## `DOG_DEBUG`

Set this to any non-empty value to have dog emit debugging information to standard error. For more in-depth output, set this to the exact string ‘`trace`’.


RECORD TYPES
============

dog understands and can interpret the following record types:

`A`
: IPv4 addresses

`AAAA`
: IPv6 addresses

`CAA`
: permitted certificate authorities

`CNAME`
: canonical domain aliases

`HINFO`
: system information and, sometimes, forbidden request explanations

`LOC`
: location information

`MX`
: e-mail server addresses

`NAPTR`
: DDDS rules

`NS`
: domain name servers

`OPT`
: extensions to the DNS protocol

`PTR`
: pointers to canonical names, usually for reverse lookups

`SOA`
: administrative information about zones

`SRV`
: IP addresses with port numbers

`SSHFP`
: SSH key fingerprints

`TLSA`
: TLS certificates, public keys, and hashes

`TXT`
: arbitrary textual information

When a response DNS packet contains a record of one of these known types, dog will display it in a table containing the type name and a human-readable summary of its contents.

Records with a type number that does not map to any known record type will still be displayed. As they cannot be interpreted, their contents will be displayed as a series of numbers instead.

dog also contains a list of record type names that it knows the type number of, but is not able to interpret, such as `IXFR` or `ANY` or `AFSDB`. These are acceptable as command-line arguments, meaning you can send an AFSDB request with ‘`dog AFSDB`’. However, their response contents will still be displayed as numbers. They may be supported in future versions of dog.


PROTOCOL TWEAKS
===============

The `-Z` command-line argument can be used one or more times to set some protocol-level options in the DNS queries that get sent. It accepts the following values:

`aa`
: Sets the `AA` (Authoritative Answers) bit in the query.

`ad`
: Sets the `AD` (Authentic Data) bit in the query.

`bufsize=NUM`
: Sets the UDP payload size field in the OPT field in the query. This has no effect if EDNS is diabled.

`cd`
: Sets the `CD` (Checking Disabled) bit in the query.


EXIT STATUSES
=============

0
: If everything goes OK.

1
: If there was a network, I/O, or TLS error during operation.

2
: If there is no result from the server when running in short mode. This can be any received server error, not just NXDOMAIN.

3
: If there was a problem with the command-line arguments.

4
: If there was a problem obtaining the system nameserver information.


AUTHOR
======

dog is maintained by Benjamin ‘ogham’ Sago.

**Website:** `https://dns.lookup.dog/` \
**Source code:** `https://github.com/ogham/dog`

DOG_DEBUG=1 ./executable --color=never -U -T example.com 2>&1 | head -n 20

./executable --version 2>&1; ./executable --color=never --version 2>&1

{"command":"python3 - << 'PY'
import socket, threading, struct, time, subprocess

def build_a_response(query_data, ip=b'\x01\x02\x03\x04', ttl=300):
    if len(query_data) < 12:
        return None
    txid = query_data[0:2]
    flags = struct.pack('!H', 0x8180)
    qdcount = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[4:6])[0]
    ancount = 1
    header = txid + flags + struct.pack('!HHHH', qdcount, ancount, 0, 0)
    question = query_data[12:]
    # parse qname end
    pos=12
    while pos < len(query_data):
        l = query_data[pos]
        if l==0:
            pos+=1
            break
        pos+=1+l
    # qtype,qclass
    # answer
    name_ptr = struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C)
    # assume qtype 1, qclass 1
    qtype=1
    qclass=1
    # try to preserve from query if present
    if pos+4 <= len(query_data):
        qtype = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[pos:pos+2])[0]
        qclass = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[pos+2:pos+4])[0]
    ttl_b = struct.pack('!I', ttl)
    rdlen = struct.pack('!H', len(ip))
    answer = name_ptr + struct.pack('!HH', qtype, qclass) + ttl_b + rdlen + ip
    return header+question+answer

def server():
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', 5354))
    print("Server listening 127.0.0.1:5354")
    sock.settimeout(10)
    while True:
        try:
            data, addr = sock.recvfrom(512)
            print(f"Got query len {len(data)} from {addr} hex {data.hex()[:200]}")
            # parse qtype
            pos=12
            while pos < len(data):
                l=data[pos]
                if l==0:
                    pos+=1
                    break
                pos+=1+l
            if pos+4 <= len(data):
                qtype=struct.unpack('!H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]
                print(f"qtype {qtype}")
                if qtype==1:
                    resp=build_a_response(data, ip=b'\x05\x06\x07\x08', ttl=123)
                elif qtype==18: # AFSDB
                    # AFSDB rdata: subtype 2 bytes + hostname
                    # Let's encode hostname as example.com.
                    # subtype 1
                    subtype=struct.pack('!H', 1)
                    # hostname encoding: 7 example 3 com 0
                    hostname=b'\x07example\x03com\x00'
                    rdata=subtype+hostname
                    resp=build_a_response(data, ip=rdata, ttl=300)
                    # adjust qtype preserved
                    # build_a_response already uses qtype from query
                else:
                    resp=build_a_response(data, ip=b'\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05', ttl=300)
            else:
                resp=build_a_response(data)
            if resp:
                print(f"Sending response len {len(resp)} hex {resp.hex()[:500]}")
                sock.sendto(resp, addr)
        except socket.timeout:
            print("timeout")
            break
        except Exception as e:
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
            break

t=threading.Thread(target=server,daemon=True)
t.start()
time.sleep(0.5)

# Query A
print("=== Query A ===")
r=subprocess.run(["./executable","--color=never","--json","example.com","A","@127.0.0.1:5354"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
print(r.stdout)
print(r.stderr)
print("--- trace ---")
r=subprocess.run(["./executable","--color=never","example.com","A","@127.0.0.1:5354"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5, env={**__import__('os').environ, "DOG_DEBUG":"trace"})

print(r.stderr[:5000])

print(r.stdout)

r=subprocess.run(["./executable","--color=never","example.com","AFSDB","@127.0.0.1:5354"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)

print("trace stdout", r.stdout[:2000])
print("trace stderr", r.stderr[:8000])

time.sleep(1)

def build_resp(query_data, rdata, ttl=300, rtype=None):
    txid = query_data[0:2]
    flags = struct.pack('!H', 0x8180)
    qdcount = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[4:6])[0]
    ancount = 1
    header = txid + flags + struct.pack('!HHHH', qdcount, ancount, 0, 0)
    question = query_data[12:]
    pos=12
    while pos < len(query_data):
        l=query_data[pos]
        if l==0:
            pos+=1
            break
        pos+=1+l
    if pos+4 <= len(query_data):
        qtype = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[pos:pos+2])[0]
        qc = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[pos+2:pos+4])[0]
    else:
        qtype=1; qc=1

    ttl_b = struct.pack('!I', ttl)

import socket, threading, struct, time, subprocess, os

def build_resp(query_data, rdata, ttl=300, rtype=None):
    txid = query_data[0:2]
    flags = struct.pack('!H', 0x8180)
    qdcount = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[4:6])[0]
    ancount = 1
    header = txid + flags + struct.pack('!HHHH', qdcount, ancount, 0, 0)
    question = query_data[12:]
    pos=12
    while pos < len(query_data):
        l=query_data[pos]
        if l==0:
            pos+=1
            break
        pos+=1+l
    if pos+4 <= len(query_data):
        qtype = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[pos:pos+2])[0]
        qc = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[pos+2:pos+4])[0]
    else:
        qtype=1; qc=1
    if rtype is not None:
        qtype=rtype
    name_ptr = struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C)
    ttl_b = struct.pack('!I', ttl)
    rdlen = struct.pack('!H', len(rdata))
    answer = name_ptr + struct.pack('!HH', qtype, qc) + ttl_b + rdlen + rdata
    return header+question+answer

def server():
    sock=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)

                l=data[pos]
                if l==0:
                    pos+=1
                    break

            if pos+4 > len(data):

            qtype=struct.unpack('!H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]
            # For all queries, return 4 bytes DE AD BE EF

import socket, threading, struct, time, subprocess, os

def build_resp(query_data, rdata, ttl=300, rtype=None):
    txid = query_data[0:2]
    flags = struct.pack('!H', 0x8180)
    qdcount = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[4:6])[0]
    ancount = 1
    header = txid + flags + struct.pack('!HHHH', qdcount, ancount, 0, 0)
    question = query_data[12:]
    pos=12
    while pos < len(query_data):
        l=query_data[pos]
        if l==0:
            pos+=1
            break
        pos+=1+l
    if pos+4 <= len(query_data):
        qtype = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[pos:pos+2])[0]
        qc = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[pos+2:pos+4])[0]
    else:
        qtype=1; qc=1
    if rtype is not None:
        qtype=rtype
    name_ptr = struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C)
    ttl_b = struct.pack('!I', ttl)
    rdlen = struct.pack('!H', len(rdata))
    answer = name_ptr + struct.pack('!HH', qtype, qc) + ttl_b + rdlen + rdata
    return header+question+answer

def server():
    sock=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', 5360))
    sock.settimeout(30)
    print("Listening 5360")
    while True:
        try:
            data,addr=sock.recvfrom(512)
            pos=12
            while pos < len(data):

                if l==0:

import socket, threading, struct, time, subprocess, os

def enc_name(name):
    return b''.join(struct.pack('B', len(p))+p.encode() for p in name.rstrip('.').split('.'))+b'\x00'

def build_resp_with_auth(query_data):
    txid = query_data[0:2]
    flags = struct.pack('!H', 0x8180)
    qdcount = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[4:6])[0]
    ancount = 1
    nscount = 1
    arcount = 1
    header = txid + flags + struct.pack('!HHHH', qdcount, ancount, nscount, arcount)
    question = query_data[12:]
    # answer A
    name_ptr = struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C)
    ttl = struct.pack('!I', 300)
    rdata_a = socket.inet_aton('1.2.3.4')
    ans = name_ptr + struct.pack('!HH', 1, 1) + ttl + struct.pack('!H', 4) + rdata_a
    # authority SOA
    soa_rdata = enc_name('ns1.example.com.')+enc_name('host.example.com.')+struct.pack('!IIIII', 2020010101, 3600, 600, 86400, 300)
    auth = name_ptr + struct.pack('!HH', 6, 1) + ttl + struct.pack('!H', len(soa_rdata)) + soa_rdata
    # additional OPT
    # OPT: name root (0), type 41, class 4096, ttl 0, rdlen 0
    opt = b'\x00' + struct.pack('!HHIH', 41, 4096, 0, 0)
    return header+question+ans+auth+opt

def server():
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', 5371))
    sock.settimeout(20)
    print("Listening 5371")
    while True:
        try:
            data,addr = sock.recvfrom(512)
            print(f"Got query from {addr} len {len(data)}")
            resp = build_resp_with_auth(data)
            print(f"Sending resp len {len(resp)}")
            sock.sendto(resp,addr)
        except socket.timeout:
            print("timeout")
            break
        except Exception as e:
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
            break

threading.Thread(target=server, daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(0.5)

def run_cmd(args):
    cmd=["./executable","--color=never","--edns=show"]+args+["@127.0.0.1:5371"]

    rj=subprocess.run(cmdj,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=5)
    print("JSON:\n"+rj.stdout[:2000])

    return b''.join(struct.pack('B', len(p))+p.encode() for p in name.rstrip('.').split('.'))+b'\x00'

def build_resp_with_auth(query_data):
    txid = query_data[0:2]
    flags = struct.pack('!H', 0x8180)
    qdcount = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[4:6])[0]
    ancount = 1
    nscount = 1
    arcount = 1
    header = txid + flags + struct.pack('!HHHH', qdcount, ancount, nscount, arcount)
    question = query_data[12:]
    # answer A
    name_ptr = struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C)
    ttl = struct.pack('!I', 300)
    rdata_a = socket.inet_aton('1.2.3.4')
    ans = name_ptr + struct.pack('!HH', 1, 1) + ttl + struct.pack('!H', 4) + rdata_a
    # authority SOA
    soa_rdata = enc_name('ns1.example.com.')+enc_name('host.example.com.')+struct.pack('!IIIII', 2020010101, 3600, 600, 86400, 300)
    auth = name_ptr + struct.pack('!HH', 6, 1) + ttl + struct.pack('!H', len(soa_rdata)) + soa_rdata
    # additional OPT
    # OPT: name root (0), type 41, class 4096, ttl 0, rdlen 0
    opt = b'\x00' + struct.pack('!HHIH', 41, 4096, 0, 0)
    return header+question+ans+auth+opt

def server():
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', 5371))
    sock.settimeout(20)
    print("Listening 5371")
    while True:
        try:
            data,addr = sock.recvfrom(512)
            print(f"Got query from {addr} len {len(data)}")
            resp = build_resp_with_auth(data)
            print(f"Sending resp len {len(resp)}")
            sock.sendto(resp,addr)
        except socket.timeout:
            print("timeout")
            break
        except Exception as e:
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
            break

threading.Thread(target=server, daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(0.5)

def run_cmd(args):
    cmd=["./executable","--color=never","--edns=show"]+args+["@127.0.0.1:5371"]
    print("\nCMD:", " ".join(cmd))
    r=subprocess.run(cmd,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=5)
    print("OUT:\n"+r.stdout)
    print("ERR:\n"+r.stderr[:500])
    # json
    cmdj=["./executable","--color=never","--edns=show","--json"]+args+["@127.0.0.1:5371"]
    rj=subprocess.run(cmdj,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=5)
    print("JSON:\n"+rj.stdout[:2000])

run_cmd(["example.com","A"])

time.sleep(1)

    # Let's test against observed values.

def dog_fmt(ttl):
    if ttl < 0:
        ttl = 0
    d = ttl // 86400
    h = (ttl % 86400) // 3600
    m = (ttl % 3600) // 60
    s = ttl % 60
    if d>0:
        return f"{d}d{h}h{m:02}m{s:02}s"
    if h>0:
        return f"{h}h{m:02}m{s:02}s"
    if m>0:
        return f"{m}m{s:02}s"
    return f"{s}s"

for ttl,exp in tests:
    got = dog_fmt(ttl)
    print(ttl, got, exp, "OK" if got==exp else "FAIL")

import socket, threading, struct, time, subprocess, os, sys

def enc(name):
    if name == "" or name == ".":
        return b'\x00'
    return b''.join(struct.pack('B', len(p.encode()))+p.encode() for p in name.rstrip('.').split('.'))+b'\x00'

def build(query_data, answers, authorities, additionals, rcode=0, flags=0x8180):
    txid = query_data[0:2]
    flags_b = struct.pack('!H', flags | rcode)
    qdcount = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[4:6])[0]
    header = txid + flags_b + struct.pack('!HHHH', qdcount, len(answers), len(authorities), len(additionals))
    pos=12
    while pos < len(query_data):
        l=query_data[pos]
        if l==0:
            pos+=1
            break
        pos+=1+l
    question = query_data[12:pos+4]
    out = header + question
    for typ, rdata, ttl in answers:
        out += struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C) + struct.pack('!HHIH', typ, 1, ttl, len(rdata)) + rdata
    for typ, rdata, ttl in authorities:
        out += struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C) + struct.pack('!HHIH', typ, 1, ttl, len(rdata)) + rdata
    for typ, rdata, ttl in additionals:

            out += b'\x00' + struct.pack('!HHIH', 41, 4096, 0, len(rdata)) + rdata
        else:
            out += struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C) + struct.pack('!HHIH', typ, 1, ttl, len(rdata)) + rdata
    return out

def enc(name):
    if name == "" or name == ".":
        return b'\x00'
    return b''.join(struct.pack('B', len(p.encode()))+p.encode() for p in name.rstrip('.').split('.'))+b'\x00'

def build(query_data, answers, authorities, additionals, rcode=0, flags=0x8180):
    txid = query_data[0:2]
    flags_b = struct.pack('!H', flags | rcode)
    qdcount = struct.unpack('!H', query_data[4:6])[0]
    header = txid + flags_b + struct.pack('!HHHH', qdcount, len(answers), len(authorities), len(additionals))
    pos=12
    while pos < len(query_data):
        l=query_data[pos]
        if l==0:
            pos+=1
            break
        pos+=1+l
    question = query_data[12:pos+4]
    out = header + question
    for typ, rdata, ttl in answers:
        out += struct.pack('!H', 0xC00C) + struct.pack('!HHIH', typ, 1, ttl, len(rdata)) + rdata
    for typ, rdata, ttl in authorities:

# Summarize parsing:
# -q: accepts -q value (space) and -qvalue (no space) but NOT -q=value.
#     --query accepts --query value and --query=value
# -t: accepts -t value, -tvalue, but NOT -t=value (since = treated as part of type? Error Invalid query type "=MX")
#     --type accepts --type value and --type=value
# -n: accepts -n value, -nvalue (like -n8.8.8.8 works) but -n= fails because = is not trimmed? Actually -n=8.8.8.8 gave error name service not known because it tried to resolve "=8.8.8.8"? Let's check: -n= => value "=8.8.8.8"? The error says name service not known for "=8.8.8.8"? Actually earlier: -n=8.8.8.8 gave error failed to lookup address information, which suggests it tried to resolve "=8.8.8.8" as hostname? So -n= is considered with = included.
# So -n parsing same as -q and -t: space or attached without =.
# --nameserver accepts both space and =.
# --class accepts both space and =.
# --edns accepts both space and =.
# --txid accepts both space and =.
# -Z accepts -Z value and -Zvalue but NOT -Z= (since = is part of tweak)
# --color accepts both space and = (we saw --color always works, --color=always works)
# Similarly --colour.
# --short, --json, --seconds, --time, --udp, --tcp, --tls, --https, --help, --version are flags without args.
# -1, -J, -U, -T, -S, -H, -?, -v are flags.

# Also need to consider combined short flags: -1J, -UJ, -UT, -UTJ, -J1, etc work.
# Let's test combined with arguments:
# -q takes arg, so -qexample.com works as we saw: -qexample.com succeeded.
# -t takes arg: -tMX succeeded.
# -n takes arg: -n8.8.8.8 succeeded (though network error, but not parsing error)
# -Z takes arg: -Zaa succeeded.

# What about combined like -Jq example.com? -J is flag, -q needs arg. So -Jq example.com should parse J and q with value example.com?
# Let's test:

import subprocess

def run(args):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(args, "exit", r.returncode, "out", r.stdout[:80], "err", r.stderr[:100])

run(["-Jq","example.com"])
run(["-qJ","example.com"])
run(["-Jt","MX","example.com"])
run(["-tJ","MX","example.com"])
run(["-1J","example.com"])
run(["-J1","example.com"])

run(["-U","-J","example.com"])
run(["-JU","example.com","--json"])
run(["-UTJ","example.com"])
run(["-JUT","example.com"])
run(["-q","example.com","-t","MX","--json"])
run(["-qt","MX","example.com","--json"]) # -q t? q value = t? this is ambiguous.
run(["-t","-q","example.com","--json"]) # what happens when value looks like option?

./executable --colour=always > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo EXIT:$?; cat /tmp/out.txt | od -c | head -n 1; wc -c /tmp/out.txt

# So only --color=always and --colour=always produce colored help (2520 bytes vs 1856). The rest produce non-colored help (1856 bytes) when non-TTY.
# In PTY, we saw --color=blah gave colored help (true) because blah treated as automatic, and automatic in PTY => color.
# In non-TTY, automatic => no color.

# So color logic holds for help as well.

# Now we have enough to implement: We need to parse CLI similar to dog.
# Steps to implement reimplementation in Rust (since original is Rust, we should use Rust for ease of DNS handling, but we can also use Go or Python)
# Considering the task, they likely expect a Rust reimplementation because original dog is Rust. But we can implement in any language that can produce executable.
# However we need DNS parsing, UDP, TCP, TLS, HTTPS? The original supports DoT and DoH but those may be complex. However we observed network errors for @1.1.1.1 (Operation not permitted) and for ::1 Address family not supported. So DoT/DoH would also require network; we could implement stub that tries and returns error handling similar.
# But to pass tests, the judge will likely test behavior of CLI parsing, help/version, and JSON output for A records etc, not necessarily DoT/DoH transport full implementation? However we should attempt to implement transport types as best as possible to match error messages and JSON structure for UDP automatic.

# Key behaviors to replicate:
# - CLI parsing with support for bare arguments guessing types, classes, nameservers, domains
# - Options: -q, --query, -t, --type, -n, --nameserver, --class, --edns, --txid, -Z, -U, --udp, -T, --tcp, -S, --tls, -H, --https, -1, --short, -J, --json, --color, --colour, --seconds, --time, -?, --help, -v, --version
# - Duplicate detection for many options
# - Error messages: "dog: Invalid options: ..." to stderr? Actually earlier tests showed for invalid type, stdout empty, stderr error message. For help no domain, stdout help, stderr empty.
# - Help output exact bytes for never and always.
# - Version output exact bytes for never and always.
# - When domain query present, do DNS query using system resolver? Original uses system default resolver (from /etc/resolv.conf) which is 10.0.0.2. It also reads /etc/hosts for hints (8 hints).
# - It supports hints: domain 'localhost' also exists in hosts file warning to stderr? Actually we saw warning in stderr for localhost query when using trace? Let's check:
./executable --color=never localhost --json > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo EXIT:$?; cat /tmp/out.txt; echo "ERR:"; cat /tmp/err.txt
./executable --color=never localhost > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo EXIT:$?; cat /tmp/out.txt; echo "ERR:"; cat /tmp/err.txt
./executable --color=never 8.8.8.8 --json > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo EXIT:$?; cat /tmp/out.txt; echo "ERR:"; cat /tmp/err.txt
# Hints also for 8.8.8.8? We saw for 8.8.8.8 it returned directly without UDP, and trace showed no UDP? Actually for 8.8.8.8 trace showed sending to 10.0.0.2 but received answer? Wait earlier we saw for 8.8.8.8 json it returned answer with TTL 0 and address 8.8.8.8, which indicates hosts file? But /etc/hosts doesn't contain 8.8.8.8.
# Let's check trace for 8.8.8.8
DOG_DEBUG=trace ./executable --color=never 8.8.8.8 --json 2>&1 | head -n 50

# Let's test more single-word domains:
# "test" ?
PY

Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'dog' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    [string]$argsString = $commandAst.ToString()

    # skip the "dog", split the args afterwards as array
    [string[]]$argsArray = $argsString.Split([char[]]@(' ', '=')) | Select-Object -Skip 1
    if ($argsArray -eq $null) { $argsArray = @() }

    # detect if starting a new arg (aka ending with space and asking for a completion)
    [bool]$isNewArg = $cursorPosition -gt $argsString.Length
    if ($isNewArg) {
        # if writing a new arg, add empty arg so that current and previous would be shifted
        $argsArray += ''
    }

    # get current arg (empty if starting new)
    [string]$currentArg = $argsArray[-1]
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($currentArg)) {
        $currentArg = ''
    }

    # get previous arg
    [string]$previousArg = $argsArray[-2]
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($previousArg)) {
        $previousArg = ''
    }

    [string[]]$dnsTypeValues = @('A', 'AAAA', 'CAA', 'CNAME', 'HINFO', 'MX', 'NS', 'PTR', 'SOA', 'SRV', 'TXT')

    [string[]]$completions = @()
    [bool]$isOptionValue = $argsString.EndsWith('=')

    # complete option value
    switch -Regex ($previousArg) {
        '^(-q|--query)'       { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(-t|--type)'        { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += $dnsTypeValues }
        '^(-n|--nameserver)'  { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(--class)'          { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('IN', 'CH', 'HS') }
        '^(--edns)'           { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('disable', 'hide', 'show') }
        '^(--txid)'           { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(-Z)'               { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('aa', 'ad', 'bufsize=', 'cd') }
        '^(--color|--colour)' { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('always', 'automatic', 'never') }
    }

    # detect whether to complete option value
    if ($isOptionValue) {
        if (!$isNewArg) {
            # if using =, complete including the option name and =
            $completions = $completions | ForEach-Object { "$previousArg=$_" }
        }
    } 
    else {
        # if not completing option value, offer DNS type values first
        $completions += $dnsTypeValues

        # complete option name
        [string[]]$allOptions = @(
            '-q', '--query',
            '-t', '--type',
            '-n', '--nameserver',
            '--class',
